description.short: Flat green tea from Mount Emei, shaped like tender bamboo leaves, with a smooth, sweet, refreshing taste
description.overview: Originating in Buddhist monasteries on Mount Emei, one of China's Four Sacred Buddhist Mountains. It remains deeply connected to Sichuan's ancient monastic tea traditions.
description.leaf: Flat, sleek, slightly curved lanceolate leaves resembling vibrant young bamboo leaves
description.aroma: Fresh, vegetal, with sweet grassy and light floral notes
description.taste: Smooth, refreshing, gently brisk, with a delicate natural sweetness
description.processing: Plucking of one bud with 1–2 tender leaves → wok fixation (shaqing) → gentle manual flattening and shaping into lanceolate leaves → low-temperature drying

history.origin: Mount Emei is one of the Four Sacred Mountains of Chinese Buddhism; tea cultivation here has been intertwined with Chan (Zen) monastic meditation for centuries
history.development: The tea's modern recipe and standardized bamboo-leaf silhouette were formally perfected in 1964, building on centuries of monastic tea culture
history.modern: Named 'Zhu Ye Qing' (Bamboo Leaf Green) by Marshal Chen Yi during his 1964 visit to Mount Emei after tasting the tea prepared by monks at Wannian Temple
interestingFacts: Mount Emei is a UNESCO World Heritage site, protecting both its sacred cultural monuments and pristine high-mountain tea ecosystems
Unlike intensely pressed flat teas like Longjing, Zhu Ye Qing is shaped with gentle pressure, preserving a graceful natural curve reminiscent of bamboo foliage
